subject: Telemetry-led slab provisioning + egress guardrails for private GPU pool
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry-led slab provisioning + egress guardrails for private GPU pool

Hi Maria / Acme ops team,

Thanks for the call last week — per our discussion attached are the telemetry extracts and a first-draft slab provisioning matrix that we think will meet your throughput targets while keeping egress within your cloud quotas. High-level summary:

- Target steady-state throughput: 85K tokens/sec across the VPC pool (all tenants combined) with 99th p50 latency target <= 200ms for short generations (<=256 tokens).
- Burst headroom: plan for 2.5x short bursts for up to 3 minutes per 10 minute window using pre-warmed slabs; measured impact on egress estimated at +18% during burst windows.
- Admission control: per-tenant token budget with dynamic reclaiming (telemetry-driven) to avoid noisy-neighbor saturation.

What we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) Confirmation of acceptable burst window (we modeled 3m/10m; you can change to 1m/5m).
2) Any existing egress hard limits from your cloud provider or network team beyond the quotas you shared.
3) Preferred failure behavior: queue+retry vs immediate fallback to hosted model (we recommend queue+retry for predictable cost).

Attached: telemetry-metrics-20260906.csv (90-day headroom distribution), slab-provisioning-matrix-v1.xlsx (candidate slab sizes and shim policies), egress-shaping-proposal.pdf (ops-friendly summary).

Next steps: if you confirm the burst window + egress limits, we'll produce a final proposal with exact slab counts per rack and an admission-control config you can upload to the private control plane.

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Ops (Acme) <ops@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry-led slab provisioning + egress guardrails for private GPU pool

Grace — thanks for the packet. Quick answers inline: 

- Burst window: 3m/10m is acceptable for now; engineering prefers 2m but ops will tolerate 3m if we can keep egress steady.
- Egress limits: our cloud account has a soft quota of 12 Gbps egress from the VPC to the internet and a firm 10 Gbps to specified partner endpoints. Anything above that requires a manual exception.
- Failure behavior: ops leans toward queue+retry, but application teams want fallback to hosted for critical user flows. Can we implement both (queue primary then fallback after X retries)?

A couple of follow ups:
1) Your telemetry extract shows 95th percentile token bursts that look higher than our historical peaks — can you explain the main drivers?
2) What are the implications for on-prem racks vs cloud-hosted racks if we later hybridize?

We are available Thurs 9/9 for a 30m follow-up; propose 10:00am PT if that works.

—Maria
SRE Lead, Acme AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry-led slab provisioning + egress guardrails for private GPU pool

Grace / Karthik — adding a few clarifications ahead of Thursday: 

> On Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700, Maria Garcia wrote:
> > Your telemetry extract shows 95th percentile token bursts that look higher than our historical peaks — can you explain the main drivers?

Short answer: burst drivers are primarily twofold in our sample set:
1) Scheduled batch inference windows where clients warm caches and prime KV stores (we detect this as short, high-qps spikes tightly coupled with specific tenant IDs).
2) Application-side retries amplified by client-side backoff misconfiguration (we see repeated identical requests within a 10s window).

Implications: slab provisioning must include a warm/reserve slab layer sized explicitly for scheduled warms + a smaller fast-evict slab for request amplification. In practice our matrix uses:
- Reserve slab (30% of pool capacity) pre-warmed and pinned to local NVMe cache.
- Dynamic slab (60% of capacity) scaled by telemetry and admission control.
- Overflow slab (10%) cold-started and used only when fallback to hosted is allowed.

On hybridizing: on-prem racks should host the reserve slab and first tier dynamic slab; cloud-hosted racks are reserved for overflow and resilient fallbacks — keeps egress predictable because we only shift traffic off-prem when overflow triggers.

Action items for Thursday:
- Grace: bring the finalized matrix with per-rack counts for both 8xA100-equivalent and 4xH100-equivalent slabs.
- Karthik: draft admission-control SLOs for per-tenant token budgets and retry thresholds.
- Maria / Acme: confirm whether the partner-endpoint 10 Gbps is a hard stop (we'll treat as firm limit until told otherwise).

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry-led slab provisioning + egress guardrails for private GPU pool

Thanks Maria / Jonas — recap + decisions from today's sync (30m):

Decisions agreed:
- Burst window set to 2m/10m (compromise to satisfy engineering and ops).
- We'll treat 10 Gbps to partner endpoints as the hard engineering constraint — Redwood will cap egress to partner endpoints and provide alerting at 8.5 Gbps.
- Failure behavior: implement queue+retry on-prem with a 3-retry exponential backoff; after 3 retries give option to fall back to hosted endpoint (configurable per tenant).
- Slab split accepted: reserve 28%, dynamic 62%, overflow 10% for initial deployment; numbers to be rounded to rack counts in the final sheet.

Open items and owners:
- Grace: produce final slab table (per-rack counts for A100/H100) and admission-control YAML to upload to the private control plane (due 2026-09-14).
- Karthik: SLO draft for per-tenant token budget and retry thresholds + runbook for eviction (due 2026-09-13).
- Maria: confirm whether Acme will accept hosted fallback for critical user flows and list any regulatory constraints (due 2026-09-12).

Attachments: included the updated slab-provisioning-matrix-v1.xlsx with provisional rack rounding and a short runbook stub for egress alert thresholds.

If no further changes by EOD Monday we'll lock these numbers and push the admission policy to the staging private control plane for validation.

Best,
Grace
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- telemetry-metrics-20260906.csv (attached)
- slab-provisioning-matrix-v1.xlsx (attached, updated)
